name: Gautham Ravichander
bio_html: Gautham leads eGov’s policy initiatives with the Government of India and partner states. He started his career at Janaagraha where he led the Ward Infrastructure Index Program and was a founding team member of The Education Alliance. Gautham has a MIB degree from The Fletcher School at Tufts University where his studies focussed on social enterprises and leveraging business models to reach underserved populations. At Fletcher, Gautham organized and co-chaired the first Tufts Innovation Symposium on Scaling Innovation in Emerging Markets.

name: Jagan Shah
bio_html:
Jagan Shah, an architect and urbanist focused on the future of cities, is currently CEO of The Infravision Foundation. A senior expert in urban development policy and practice at Artha Global, he has over two decades of experience in India’s urban sector across consultancy, teaching, writing, and public speaking.

From 2013 to 2019, he served as Director of the National Institute of Urban Affairs, where he led evidence-based policy and planning support for urban local bodies, state governments, and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. His work spanned areas such as smart cities, e-governance, spatial planning, water and sanitation, municipal finance, transit-oriented development, and sustainability.

He is a Board Member at Clean Air Asia India, and has previously worked with the World Bank and as a Resident Senior Fellow at the IDFC Institute.

name: Jaya Dhindaw
bio_html:
Jaya is an urban development professional and researcher with over two decades of global experience in sustainable development, urban resilience and natural resource management. She provides strategic leadership to all urban development, planning and resilience initiatives across WRI India and is currently the Executive Program Director, Sustainable Cities and Director, WRI India Ross Center. Prior to WRI India, Jaya worked for the Centre for Infrastructure, Sustainable Transport and Urban Planning (CISTUP) at the Indian Institute of Science, leading the urban planning and infrastructure development team.

A published author, Jaya earned her undergraduate degree in architecture from the University of Pune and holds a Master’s in City Planning from the Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur. She also studied community planning, with a focus on environmental policy and planning, from the University of Cincinnati. In addition to her WRI India commitments, Jaya serves as a Managing Associate Editor for the Journal of Sustainable Urbanization, Planning and Progress (Whioce Publishing, Singapore).

name: Kuldeep Dantewadia
bio_html:
Co-Founder & CEO of Reap Benefit, Kuldeep Dantewadia has been pivotal in building a movement of public problem solving among adolescents & youth. Inspired by his father’s passion for Bangalore’s environmental issues, he was driven to solve environmental & civic problems. An ambitious train journey, Jagriti Yatra, a confluence of change-makers, youth leaders, problem-solvers & innovators, further ignited his entrepreneurial journey.

A strong ethical leader, Kuldeep has won several accolades including Ashoka’s Lead Changemaker, MIT’s Global Startup Weekend, Changelooms Fellowship, S3IDF Fellowship, StartingBloc Fellowship, and Architects of the Future. Under his leadership, Reap Benefit embarked on several initiatives creating new methods of environmental education and problem-solving.

name: Madhav Pai
bio_html:
Madhav Pai is a respected thinker-practitioner in urbanization, climate change, transportation, and environment. He joined WRI India in 2008 as part of its founding team and has played a key role in building high-performance teams to design and scale solutions for India’s complex urban challenges.

A civil engineer from the University of Mumbai, Madhav earned a Master’s in Transport Planning from UC Berkeley. He applies systems thinking to address the complexities of contemporary cities. Under his leadership at WRI India Ross Center and previously at EMBARQ India, his team has advanced pioneering initiatives including the Mumbai Climate Action Plan, Raahgiri street campaigns, and the National Electric Bus Program, while shaping policy on urban transport, clean air, and sustainable planning.

name: Milind Mhaske
bio_html: Milind has anchored Praja since 2010 scaling it up to become a key national player in transforming urban governance across India. He helped set up some of its key projects: report cards for ranking elected representatives, training programs for elected representatives and Praja’s Urban Governance Index in 2020. He is a business management graduate from Mumbai University and brings more than two decades of experience in managing development sector projects.

name: Pratima Joshi
bio_html:
A practitioner for over 25 years, Pratima has constantly been using her knowledge to further Shelter Associates’ cause. She conceptualised the intricacies of what participative design would look like on the ground for both housing and sanitation and built the sensitivity required for bringing multiple stakeholders together on a single project. Strongly believing in sharing knowledge, Pratima regularly speaks and presents her work across the world, participates in policy discussions and plays advisory roles in government programs such as the Rajiv Awas Yojana.

Pratima was a recipient of an Aga Khan scholarship for her master’s in architecture, building design for developing countries, at the Bartlett School of Architecture and Planning, London. She is the only Indian to receive the ‘Google Earth Hero Award’. An Ashoka fellow, she is recognized by BBC as a leading ‘Slum architect of India’.

name: Pritika Hingorani
bio_html:
Pritika Hingorani is the Chief Executive Officer at Artha India. In addition to her management responsibilities, she also leads Artha’s work on urbanisation and emerging cities. Pritika was a Research Fellow and Director at the IDFC Institute in Mumbai. Previously, she spent several years at the IDFC Policy Group where she worked on projects spanning affordable housing, water, sanitation and rural development. Prior to IDFC, Pritika spent three years as an Associate working across the International Trade, Financial Economics and Antitrust practices with Charles River Associates, in Washington DC and London.

Pritika has a Masters in City Planning from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. She has a dual Bachelors degree in Economics and Political Science (Honours) from Bryn Mawr College, with a minor in Peace and Conflict studies.

name: Shilpa Kumar
bio_html:
Based in Mumbai, Shilpa oversees British International Investment’s operations in India, delivering climate finance and investments for inclusive growth. She brings over 30 years of leadership experience in banking, financial services, and social impact investing.

Previously a Partner at Omidyar Network India, she directed strategy and investments across Responsible Tech, Cities & Climate, and Inclusive Property, and led financial inclusion policy work. She also held senior roles at ICICI Bank, including MD & CEO of ICICI Securities, and has served on multiple boards and industry committees.

name: Shubhagato Dasgupta
bio_html:
Shubhagato Dasgupta is a Senior Fellow at the Centre for Policy Research (CPR) and head of the Scaling City Institutions for India (Sci-Fi) Sanitation initiative. His current research focuses on drinking water and sanitation in India and the world, with particular reference to flagship government programs and service delivery challenges in smaller cities. Other major areas of work include urban infrastructure and service delivery financing, housing and slum rehabilitation, urban sector public finance, and urban environmental infrastructure planning, management, and investment alternatives.

Before joining CPR, Shubhagato led the Support to National Policies for Urban Poverty Reduction project, a collaboration between the UK’s Department for International Development (DFID) and India’s Ministry of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation to develop pro-poor urban policies in 20 cities across 15 states.

Shubhagato Dasgupta was trained as an architect at the Centre for Environmental Planning and Technology in Ahmedabad and holds an MSc in housing and development planning from the Development Planning Unit of the University College London. He is also currently undertaking a PhD at the Centre for Urban Studies at the University of Amsterdam.

name: Srikanth Viswanathan
bio_html: In his role as Chief Executive Officer, Srikanth steers the strategy with an oversight on operations. Srikanth joined Janaagraha in 2011 and prior to this role was head of Advocacy and Reforms. Srikanth is an Associate member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India with professional work experience in banking and audit. Prior to Janaagraha worked with Standard Chartered Bank and KPMG for 10 years.

name: Viraj Tyagi
bio_html:
Viraj Tyagi is the CEO of eGov Foundation. He is passionate about the impact of a jugalbandi of Digital Public Goods, policies, and ecosystems in solving complex societal problems at scale and speed. Before joining the impact sector, Viraj was an entrepreneur and corporate leader with wide-ranging experience in building large businesses in Europe and India. He is a serial entrepreneur, an active investor in start-ups, and a mentor to entrepreneurs.

Prior to eGov, Viraj was the CEO and co-founder of NettPositive – one of the first Big Data and Analytics companies in India. He is also a co-founder of the fintech start-up – Finnable. He is on the board of several start-ups and companies. He is an alumnus of the Indian Institute of Management – Bangalore (IIM-B) and the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT – BHU).

name: Champaka Rajagopal
bio_html:
Champaka Rajagopal is a senior researcher, educator, practitioner, focused on urban policy, governance, planning and infrastructure governance. She is a Fellow at the Centre for Policy Research, India, Professor Affiliae at the Urban School, SciencesPo, Paris, France, Founder, Director of The Entrepreneurship and Partnerships Lab. She also serves as Trustee on the Board of Trustees, IJURR Foundation, UK.

Her research interests lie in investigating state-business relationships, firms, entrepreneurship and innovation, with a focus on commercial and contract laws, policies, governance, mechanisms directed at privatisation. She draws on experiential learning from her more than two decades of engagement with multi-national corporations and international finance institutions, in India and abroad.

Previously, as part of international consultancy firms, she co-led large statutory plans, including the Draft Development Plan for Greater Mumbai 2034 and Revised Master Plan 2015, Bangalore, where the focus was to remove regulatory rigidity and regulatory capture. In her two decades of practice across cities in the global South and the North, with international donors, national-state governments, businesses, markets and communities she has advanced the design of policies, regulatory processes, instruments and mechanisms that deepen democratic processes and respond to place.

name: Dhanashree Gurav
bio_html: Dhanshree Gurav is the Associate Executive Director at Shelter Associates. Dhanshree has been championing the right of women to access safe sanitation and sustainable menstruation for a decade. With the soul of an environmentalist, she applies the sustainability lens to all the Shelter Associates’ sanitation-related interventions. She is a professional with a Bachelors in commerce focused in Social Work from the College of Social Work Nirmala Niketan, Mumbai.

name: Krishnan Subbaraman
bio_html: Krishnan leads strategy and partnerships at Janaagraha. He works closely with the CEO to implement the organizational strategy and operating model, scope and anchor institutional partnerships, support organization development initiatives and to watch emerging trends and shape Janaagraha’s response to them over the medium and long term. Prior to this, he was part of the early leadership team at Central Square Foundation, where he spent 8+ years working at the intersection of governments, non-profits, researchers and funders to drive system-led reform in India’s school education sector. His commitment to the development sector was seeded through the Teach for India fellowship, where he led a class of 45 students in an under-resourced school towards academic and social success as a full-time teacher for 2 years. He started his career with a short stint in Infrastructure Project Finance at Axis Bank. Krishnan holds an MBA in Finance and Economics from XLRI, Jamshedpur and is a gold medalist in Instrumentation and Control Engineering from NIT, Trichy.

name: Mayura Gadkari
bio_html:
Mayura Gadkari is a Principal at the Centre for Emerging Cities (ACES) at Artha Global. Prior to joining Artha, Mayura was with the National Institute of Urban Affairs, anchored with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India. During her 12+ years of professional experience, she has worked with diverse stakeholders within the distinct governance levels across urban India- the town, city, region, state and at the national level by being a part of international non-profits, para-governmental organisations and projects financially supported by multi-laterals and bi-laterals. As an Urban Development Practitioner, Mayura has conducted research on an array of topics, delivered talks at several academic and research institutions, seminars and conferences in India and abroad.

Mayura holds a Bachelor’s degree in Architecture from the University of Mumbai and a Master’s degree in Architecture from CEPT University, Ahmedabad.

name: Meghna Bandelwar Indurkar
bio_html: Meghna has over 6 years of experience working in the Urban sector. She has worked as an architect in design and planning of residential complexes in Mumbai, and has been associated with Praja Foundation for the last 4 years, managing the research and advocacy efforts with Union and State Governments in India. She was also instrumental in planning, executing and launching Praja’s Urban Governance Index. She is a graduate in architecture from Mumbai University and Master of Technology in Urban Development and Management from TERI School of Advanced Studies.

name: Neha Lal
bio_html:
Neha Lal is Senior Manager, Urban Development in the Sustainable Cities and Transport team at WRI India. Here she works on research and implementation projects related to systems thinking for urban challenges, land governance and policy, strategic regional planning, and climate resilience. Neha currently manages the Thriving Eco city-regions Initiative and supports efforts towards on building regenerative development trajectories across multiple city regions in India. Previously, she has contributed to initiatives on strategic projects in Delhi NCR, land use integration policies and planning for transitioning urban villages.

Neha has previously held research positions with Mahila Housing SEWA Trust, an advocacy organization and NGO working on participatory governance and habitat upgradation; Indian Institute for Human Settlements (IIHS), a research and educational institution working on sustainable urban transformation; and Observer Research Foundation, a leading policy research think tank. She has also served as an editorial team member of anthropological journal Architecture_MPS, published by UCL Press. Neha’s work has been published in Springer, Development Informatic Working paper series and MHT-SEWA research publications.

name: Sarah Misra
bio_html:
Sarah Misra is currently Senior Director of Fundraising & Partnerships at Reap Benefit. A Special Education professional with a double degree in English Literature and Education, she is also the Founder of a chain of Schools, Chrysalis High where she set up 5 inclusive K12 schools across Bangalore.

Before joining Reap Benefit she was the Chief Learning Officer at Hippocampus Learning Centres, where she headed the school division of 20 schools in Karnataka; empowering teachers and students in underserved communities. She finds joy in creating opportunities for children and youth to explore, learn and find themselves and has committed herself to removing the barriers to education and learning at the grassroots level.

name: Siddharth Pandit
bio_html:
Siddharth comes with a varied background in urban development and a lifelong commitment to learning and working in the urban sector. Coming from humble beginnings as the son of a cab driver in Mumbai, Siddharth’s journey has taken him across major cities, including Boston, Jakarta, Shanghai, New York, Paris, New Delhi, and now Pune, where he is based.

Siddharth is a development professional with 20+ years of experience in building teams and organisations focused on improved capacity, governance and infrastructure in the urban sector. He has also led teams in improving personnel management to deliver improved functionary outcomes of government officials. He has a deep immersive experience that includes designing and managing national urban missions, collaborating with diverse stakeholders such as city governments, local communities, and multilateral agencies, and spearheading initiatives in smart city planning, housing, transportation policy, and community participation.

Siddharth’s professional journey spans across strategic, operational, and leadership positions in the private, public, and non-profit sectors. He brings to U-CAN a unique blend of skills as a technologist, geographer, and urban planner, coupled with an inspiration with the idea of fostering creative energies and mutually adaptive learning processes to improve the lives in Indian cities.

name: Akshay Agarwal
bio_html: Akshay leads program delivery at U-CAN, and works closely with the CEO and the secretariat in planning and executing U-CAN’s various activities. He has extensive experience working on various aspects of India’s development aspirations as well as global development initiatives, spending nearly seven years working in India’s nascent public policy space, providing policy advice, drafting communication and advocacy material, planning documents for government agencies, and analysing key policies at national and sub-national levels. He has also been part of the founding team of a global organisation’s Asia team, with a strong focus on urban transformation.

name: Manali Shah
bio_html: Manali is a facilitator and change practitioner with experience across organizations such as BullzI Inc, AJK Mass Communication Research Centre, Friedrich Naumann Foundation, VSO GIVE Network, and Sir Ratan Tata Trust. Her work focuses on enabling alignment and collaboration through purpose, values, vision, and stakeholder engagement. She is certified in Organizational Change Facilitation and has been trained in facilitation and strategic planning by organizations in India and Germany. Manali has been closely associated with U-CAN, contributing to building meaningful collaboration within the network.
